items.title: Inside Amaravati’s pioneering leap to quantum frontier
points: Andhra Pradesh State Quantum Mission Director C.V.
Sridhar and L Venkata Subramaniam CEO of Qbit Force and Srsti Quantum discussing at the quantum lab at Medha Towers in Gannnavaram. | Photo Credit: K.V.S.
Giri For decades, advanced quantum hardware belonged exclusively to a handful of elite Western and East Asian laboratories.
In this expensive, closed-off club, developing nations remained spectators or mere end users.
In Amaravati, engineers and policymakers are working to upend that hierarchy.

Starting from scratch, the Amaravati Quantum Valley (AQV) is turning a greenfield blueprint into South Asia’s premier deep tech hub, betting that India shouldn’t just use quantum computers; it should build them.
That ambition traces back to Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu, whose push for frontier technology in Amaravati looked well beyond buying a foreign supercomputer.

Tanker sinks river cruise ship in New Orleans collision
points: The 17,764 dwt bitumen tanker Atlantic Asphalt has struck and sunk a river cruise ship on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, leaving 32 people hospitalised and prompting a major emergency response.

The collision occurred at approximately 12.30 pm local time on November 13, when the 2017-built tanker struck American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage, which was docked at the Port of New Orleans and disembarking passengers.
The impact caused the riverboat to take on water and capsize, with emergency services launching a rescue operation involving the US Coast Guard, port authorities and nearby vessels.
New Orleans mayor Helena Moreno confirmed that all 180 passengers and crew had been accounted for.
According to VesselsValue, the Atlantic Asphalt is owned by single-ship company Nave Shipping and operated by Swiss company Asphaltos Trade.

The US Coast Guard closed a section of the Mississippi River between mile markers 93 and 96 while emergency operations continued, temporarily affecting commercial vessel traffic through the busy shipping corridor.
